subject: Possible to output R code that Shiny runs?

messages.author: abd88ec3abd811ad
messages.subject: Possible to output R code that Shiny runs?
parts:
I have a rather extensive Shiny app, the main purpose of which is to provide social science researchers with a specific set of analysis tools without requiring knowledge of the R command line. Since it would be impossible to capture all of the power and flexibility of R in a web app (though Shiny has been very impressive so far), I would like to provide my users with the option of transitioning into the command line. Specifically, I want them to be able to see the R code that Shiny runs as a result of their interaction with the app.

Is there any functionality in Shiny or other packages that would allow me to do this?

I am aware of the shinyAce package: https://github.com/trestletech/shinyAce
which is a viable option, except that it would require me to call updateAceEditor("editorid", value="newcode...") anytime one of my reactive objects changes. I would be re-writing code that already exists, almost doubling the length of my server.R file.

Ideally, I'm looking for something that can capture the R commands that shiny runs as they happen and recognize when they change. Does this exist?

Thanks,
Emily

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Re: Possible to output R code that Shiny runs?
parts: I don't think I would want all code run to show up. Tends to get pretty messy, at least for me. However, when I am 'done' with a model or analysis I have an option to write the function calls used for that analysis to am Rmd document in a shinyAce input . Note that these call are to 'regular' functions. When the user interacts with the app normally the functions are called by reactives. When the users wants to replicate the analysis they call the regular functions directly by knit-ing the Rmd document from within the app.

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Re: Possible to output R code that Shiny runs?
parts:
Hi Emily,

Below the basic structure  I currently use for various tools. You generate the ui elements as usual. Then there is a main reactive that calls a regular function to do the main analysis. The reactive calls a function with elements from input as needed, sort-of like a reactive-wrapper. Each of the analysis tools I have creates a summary of results and plots. These functions take the output from the main analysis as input (either through a reactive or not). The code skeleton is probably clearer than I can explain it in words (see below).

The full code is on github (https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant). Look in dev/base for the simplest parts. The structure still feels messy to me so any suggestions on how to simplify are welcome. For example, passing the input-values to functions is a little onerous. Perhaps putting inputs into a reactiveValue as a list and/or using makeReactiveBinding (e.g., https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/7TW5OchNjc8)? Ideas for improvement welcome!

Vincent

output$uiTool_var <- renderUI({
# variable selection
  vars <- varnames()
isNum <- "numeric" == getdata_class() | "integer" == getdata_class()
  vars <- vars[isNum]
  if(length(vars) == 0) return()
  selectInput(inputId = "tool_var", label = "Variable (select one):", choices = vars, 
   selected = state_singlevar("tool_var",vars), multiple = FALSE)
})

output$ui_tool <- renderUI({
# for ui
  list(
   wellPanel(
   uiOutput("uiTool_var")
   ),
  helpAndReport('The tool','tool',includeHTML("tools/help/tool.html"))
  )
})

output$tool <- renderUI({
# for input-output
  statTabPanel("Menu", "The tool", ".tool", "tool", widthFun = "plotWidth", heightFun = "plotHeight")
  # can insert custom functions for plotWidth and plotHeight
})

.tool <- reactive({
# reactive that calls the function for main analysis
# . used to indicate this is an 'internal' function
tool()
})

tool <- function(datasets, ...) {
# function for main analysis

  ...

  result <- list()

  ... 

  return(result)
}
})

# Generate output for the summary tab
summary_tool <- function(result = .tool()) {

}

# Generate output for the plots tab
plots_tool <- function(result = .tool()) {

}
